q-36941:
A function is invertible on a particular interval if and only if it's a one-to-one function on that interval. To determine the intervals on which the function is invertible, we use the horizontal line test.

- The given function is invertible on the interval $x\in (-2,0].$ Indeed, a horizontal line will intersect the curve at most once, no matter where we draw the line.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13932058/assets/d7c6e8d314483ad67e89ce5d4675b7af27fa08c88a4ed9d95eed9ad2a4da51cc.png)

- The given function is **not** invertible on the intervals $x\in (-2,2]$ and $x\in [-4,-2]\cup [2,4]$ because some horizontal lines will intersect the curve more than once.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13932058/assets/cee829f7e3d5f32b0acb54cb5c40406d8391d2a2967c68df0c1f5e1cae87d729.png)

Therefore, the correct answer is "I only".

q-36004:
A function is invertible on a particular interval if and only if it's a one-to-one function on that interval. To determine the intervals on which the function is invertible, we use the horizontal line test.  

- The given function is invertible on each of the intervals $x\in [-6,0]$ and $x\in [4,10).$ Indeed, any horizontal line will intersect the curve at most once, no matter where we draw the line.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13932058/assets/7cb282e3fa66af801ff03816973d5f5f1d0cb41e39d08a8addd27d7aa9c5b9df.png)

      

- The given function is **not** invertible on the interval $[-6,4]$  because some horizontal lines will intersect the curve more than once.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13932058/assets/000953609a7b3e13ad09473ead62f96aa895c7f94aa618884e69883595004fd4.png)

 

 Therefore, the correct answer is "I  and III only".

q-66725:
The function $f(x)$ is a linear function with slope $-1$ and $y$-intercept $3,$ as shown below. 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13932058/assets/aaa05d1ab0fd630dacd81723fe00472cb901fb6f73af5f111f44459476191c0f.png)

A function is invertible on a particular interval if and only if it's a one-to-one function on that interval. To determine the intervals on which the function is invertible, we use the horizontal line test.

- The given function is invertible on the interval $x\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ On this interval, a horizontal line will intersect the curve at most once, no matter where we draw the line.

- Since the function is invertible on $x\in (-\infty ,\infty ),$ it is also invertible on  $x\in (0.5,\infty )$ and $x\in [-3,\sqrt{2}].$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I, II, and III".

q-66669:
The graph of the function $f(x)=(x-2)^{2},$ can be obtained in the following way:

1\. Take the curve $y={x}^{2}.$

2\. Translate it by $2$ units  to  the right  $f(x)=(x-2)^{2}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13932058/assets/1e3ac550e35a3dc93b3e26e5834f763847b04f5133de02e368124f54dd2b9dd6.png)

A function is invertible on a particular interval if and only if it's a one-to-one function on that interval. To determine the intervals on which the function is invertible, we use the horizontal line test.

- The function $f(x)$ is not invertible on the interval $x\in (-1,5).$ On this interval, some horizontal lines will intersect the curve more than once.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13932058/assets/3ebb316ca122b6786b8ef501fc7c56f8e0e68c8cfc32e5801c493d38382fc26c.png)

- The function $f(x)$ is invertible on the intervals $x\in (2,\infty )$  and $x\in (-\infty ,2].$  On these intervals, any horizontal line will intersect the curve at most once, no matter where we draw the line.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13932058/assets/86c7c9cacc7a3868565f33130563ffed0ca423aa087e76cc08d103ea171822ed.png)

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and III only".
